blocking_findings: COLD-R02-B1: PROCEDURE.md run commands referenced the superseded -R01 experiment directories; run_id is derived from the config filename, so the runs would have been attributed to the wrong revision and the reviewed -R02 artifacts would never have executed

COLD-R02-B2: PROCEDURE.md documented no finalize_decision/authorize_experiment step, so finalization.json and authorization.json - without which run-remote.sh refuses to start - were not producible from the procedure alone
rationale: Revision 2 fixed all three revision-1 blockers (verified independently by the cold_start reviewer) but was itself BLOCKed by the same reviewer with two further real defects, both re-verified by the producer before acting: COLD-R02-B1 the hash-bound procedure still named the superseded revision-1 experiment directories, so following it literally would have executed revision-1 configs and, because run-remote.sh derives the run id from the config filename, attributed the runs to the wrong revision; COLD-R02-B2 the procedure never documented how the finalization and authorization are produced, so the mandated ordering was not achievable from the procedure alone. The satellite_drl review passed revision 2. A third revision is therefore required, with a new experiment_id so revision 2's compiled artifacts stay intact rather than being replaced in place.
revision_instructions: Generate every run command's experiment id from the revision's own compiled ids, and add a self-check that no run command references an earlier revision
Add a mandatory section documenting reviews -> decision -> finalization -> authorization with the exact commands and their expected sentinels
Emit tolerance_contract_s from the witness and selftest reports too, so the claim that it is emitted by every report is literally true
Make witness fail loud on a missing or empty decision log instead of reporting an admissible-looking zero-row witness
